 Hon'Ble Mrs Justice Surepalli Nanda

Order:

Heard the learned counsel appearing on behalf of the petitioners and the Learned Government Pleader for Revenue, appearing on behalf of respondent Nos.1 to 4 and Sri A.Venkateshwar Rao,
learned Counsel appearing on behalf of respondent No.5.
2. PERUSED THE RECORD.
3. The petitioner approached the Court seeking the relief as follows:
"to issue an Writ Order or direction more particularly one in the nature of Writ of Mandamus declaring the action of the Respondent Nos.1 to 4 are not considering the representation dated 12.05.2022 of the petitioners for compensation amount in respect of Land an extent of Ac:1.27 gts., in Sy.No.297/5/2A on the names of the Palakurhti Dasu and Palakurhti Samuel vide District Colelctor Khammam File No.G1/790/2020, dated 11.05.2021, RDO/LAO/Kalluru File No.A/232/2020 dated 22.04.2021 and Gazette Notification no.A3/18/2021, dated 11.05.2021 and pursuance to the consent Deed SN,J WP_6901_2023 dated 11.05.2020, though the petitioners are having right in the Land as highly illegal and arbitrary and consequently direct the Respondent Nos.1 to 4 to consider the representation dated 12.05.2022 of the Petitioners for compensation award as award passed earlier, along with the Respondent No.5 vide Rc.No.C/369/2020, dated 30.04.2020 RDO and LAO Kalluru and by passing final orders and pass such other/orders as it may deem fit and necessary in the circumstances of the case."

4. This Court vide its Interim Orders, dated 11.04.2023 observed as follows:
"Notice Before Admission.
Learned Assistant Government Pleader for Land Acquisition takes notice for Respondent Nos. 1 to 4.

sentences.text: Learned Counsel for the petitioners is permitted to take out personal notice to respondent no.5 by 'RPAD' and file proof of service in the Registry by the next date of hearing.

From the written instructions placed before this Court, it is noticed that respondent no.3 has concluded to pay compensation in favour of respondent No.5 for an extent of Ac.1.21  guntas though the names of the petitioners were shown in the preliminary notification as well as in the declaration made under Section 19(1) of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (for short, 'the Act, 2013').

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Thus, there appears to be conflicting claims for receiving compensation in respect of the said extent of land.

But, respondent No.3, instead of referring the matter to the authority under Section 64 of the Act, 2013 for deciding entitlement of SN,J WP_6901_2023 compensation of the petitioners or respondent No.5, has concluded to pay compensation in favour of respondent No.5

In the circumstances, pending further orders, there shall be interim direction directing respondent Nos. 1 to 4 not to disburse the compensation in respect of the subject land till next date of hearing.

5. Taking into consideration the representation made by the petitioner dated 12.05.2022 for payment of equal compensation amount to the petitioner along with Respondent No.5 and two others in respect of land to an extent of AC:No.1.27 gts., in Sy.No.297/5/2A, being joint family property on the names of the petitioner i.e. Palakurhti Samuel and Palakurthi Dasu the 5th respondent herein and two others i.e. Palakurti Krishnaiah and Palakurti Adinarayana being the four sons of late Kondaiah in view of the fact of the said subject land being notified under Gazettee notification No.A3/08/2021 dated 11.05.2021 for acquisition of the land for the purpose of Railway line for transporting of Singareni Coal from Sathupalli, the writ petition is disposed off directing the respondents 1 to 4 to consider petitioner's representation dated 12.05.2022, SN,J WP_6901_2023 in accordance to law, within a period of two weeks from the date of receipt of the copy of this order,
and duly communicate the said decision to the petitioners.
6. Till respondent Nos.1 to 4 take a decision on the representation of the petitioner, dated 12.05.2022, the interim orders passed by this Court on 11.04.2023 shall remain in force.

However,
there shall be no order as to costs.
Miscellaneous petitions, if any, pending shall stand closed.
